articles.title: Kay Adams causes huge stir with Super Bowl 61 prediction: “They're killing me”
articles.standfirst: Adams’ Bears-Broncos Super Bowl prediction gets roasted by NFL fans
articles.summary: Adams’ Bears-Broncos Super Bowl prediction gets roasted by NFL fans
articles.body:
NFL host Kay Adams is standing by a Bears-Broncos matchup despite a wave of skepticism, with most of the criticism aimed squarely at Chicago rather than Denver.

Adams knew her Super Bowl LXI prediction was aggressive. What she didn't expect was just how quickly NFL fans would turn it into a debate.

The FanDuel TV host has picked the Chicago Bears to face the Denver Broncos at SoFi Stadium, a matchup that immediately drew pushback because of how far Adams believes Chicago can go.

“I’m getting killed for my Super Bowl teams,” Adams told Rob Gronkowski.

“I said Bears vs Broncos . But I’m getting crushed and it’s not about the Broncos, which obviously, best defense, maybe Bo Nix can pull it out. Sean Payton. People are really killing me on the Bears.”

Then she put the question directly to Gronkowski : “How bad is my Super Bowl pick?”

Denver is easier to defend

The Broncos are coming off a 14-3 season and a trip to the AFC Championship Game, which makes Adams ’ confidence in Denver easier to understand. She's also been vocal about how highly she rates the roster.

“The [Broncos have the] most complete roster already in the NFL, and then they bring in, which is somehow still being slept on, Jaylen Waddle,” Adams said.

“I cannot for the life of me understand why this team is getting the eighth-longest odds in the conference right now.”

Adams isn't alone in that assessment. ESPN’s Dan Orlovsky has also argued that Denver is being overlooked despite finishing as the AFC’s No.1 seed last season.

“This roster is absolutely loaded,” Orlovsky said. “They are the best team that, for some reason, we are constantly overlooking.”

That makes Chicago the real swing factor in Adams ’ prediction.

Bears pick has fans pushing back

Some fans believe the Bears ’ 2025 success will be difficult to repeat, while others think Chicago is being dismissed too easily.

“The Bears are going to show all y’all that it wasn’t all some mysterious apparition happening last season,” one fan wrote. “They have a top-notch coach with a quarterback that has that clutch gene everyone talks about.”

Another pointed to Caleb Williams ’ late-game play even before Chicago’s recent rise: “I mean year one with Caleb he led a lot of drives late in game that were foiled by terrible coaching decisions,” the fan wrote.

Another fan rejected the idea that last season should simply be written off as a one-off run. “Saying last year was magical without even making the Super Bowl and then saying it doesn’t happen two years in a row is almost hater type talk,” the fan said.

That is ultimately the bet Adams is making. Denver has already shown it can reach the final stages of the AFC race. Chicago still has to prove it belongs in that same category. Adams is betting that 2026 is the year it does.

articles.title: Justin Bieber and Harry Styles the frontrunners for 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show... but there's a major drawback
articles.standfirst: Roc Nation reportedly has two global superstars in mind for SoFi Stadium
articles.summary: Roc Nation reportedly has two global superstars in mind for SoFi Stadium
articles.body:
The Super Bowl halftime show has become as much a global entertainment event as a football spectacle, and the NFL may be aiming particularly high for 2027.

Justin Bieber and Harry Styles are reportedly among the leading names on Roc Nation’s wish list for Super Bowl LXI, which will be played Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

TMZ reports that both artists are high on the list being considered by Roc Nation, the entertainment company founded by Jay-Z that works with the NFL on its live music strategy.

There is, however, an important distinction between being wanted and being booked.

Neither Bieber nor Styles has reportedly been formally approached about performing, and TMZ suggested both could ultimately decline even if offers are made.

That leaves the NFL with an intriguing early shortlist but no confirmed headliner.

Bieber already has experience

Bieber would arrive with relatively recent experience performing around one of the world’s biggest sporting events.

The Canadian singer appeared during halftime entertainment at the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, part of a first-of-its-kind show that generated debate because soccer traditionally has a far shorter halftime break than the NFL.

Reaction to Bieber ’s appearance was mixed, including discussion over his song selection, but the setting provided another reminder of the scale of audience he can command. A Super Bowl performance would be very different.

Halftime entertainment is deeply embedded in the NFL’s championship event, and artists frequently use the platform as a way to reach hundreds of millions of viewers while giving their catalog a major commercial boost.

The NFL doesn't traditionally pay its halftime performer a standard appearance fee, although production expenses are covered. The value instead comes from exposure, with streaming numbers, ticket demand and music sales often surging around the performance.

SoFi Stadium adds more expectation

The location only increases the pressure on whoever eventually gets the call. The last Super Bowl held at SoFi Stadium featured a blockbuster halftime lineup of Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige, Kendrick Lamar and 50 Cent .

That show became one of the most memorable halftime productions of recent years and set a high bar for the event’s return to Los Angeles.

Styles would bring a different energy, combining his One Direction fan base with a hugely successful solo career. Bieber would offer similar global reach, with a catalog spanning more than a decade of mainstream pop.

The NFL usually announces its halftime performer around late September, meaning a decision could come relatively soon. Until then, Bieber and Styles remain high-profile possibilities rather than actual bookings.

The NFL may know who it wants, but the harder part could be convincing either one to take the stage.

articles.title: Jay-Z left scrambling for Super Bowl headliner after Macklemore pro-Palestine controversy
articles.standfirst: The fallout from Macklemore’s pro-Palestinian remarks has reportedly complicated plans for the NFL’s biggest musical event
articles.summary: The fallout from Macklemore’s pro-Palestinian remarks has reportedly complicated plans for the NFL’s biggest musical event
articles.body:
Jay-Z is reportedly facing an unexpected challenge as plans for the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show enter a crucial stage, with the fallout from Macklemore’s pro-Palestinian remarks adding another layer of sensitivity around the event.

The NFL and Jay-Z’s Roc Nation have yet to announce the performer for Super Bowl LXI, which will be held at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, 2027.

A report citing a source familiar with the discussions claims organizers are struggling to secure a headliner, raising the possibility that Jay-Z could take the stage himself alongside several guest artists. The claim hasn’t been confirmed by the NFL or Roc Nation.

Jay-Z has helped oversee the halftime lineup since Roc Nation became involved with the NFL in 2019, but he hasn’t performed in the slot himself. His potential involvement comes as artists face increased scrutiny over the political dimensions of major live events.

Macklemore fallout adds pressure

The latest concerns follow Macklemore’s removal from Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour after the rapper made pro-Palestinian comments during a September 4 performance at MetLife Stadium.

According to reports, stadium owners raised concerns about hosting Macklemore following his remarks, ultimately leading to his departure from the remaining dates.

Sheeran later said the decision to remove Macklemore wasn’t his, while explaining that he prefers to keep politics away from his professional platform. He said his shows are intended to bring together audiences from different backgrounds rather than serve as political forums.

The controversy escalated when the other scheduled support acts - Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga - also withdrew from the remaining concerts. Macklemore has since announced plans to donate $1 million in net earnings from the tour to organizations providing aid to Palestinians.

The dispute has also produced a notable shift in the secondary ticket market. TicketData reported that the cheapest resale ticket for Macklemore’s October concert at Red Rocks in Colorado climbed from $108 to $157 over three days, representing a 45% increase.

The company attributed the unusual surge to the events surrounding his removal from Sheeran’s tour.

Meanwhile, resale prices for nine of Sheeran’s 10 remaining venues declined. TicketData cautioned, however, that falling prices are common as concert dates approach, meaning the changes can’t automatically be linked to the controversy.

The episode could make potential performers more cautious about accepting one of entertainment’s biggest stages. The Super Bowl halftime show is unpaid, according to reporting, meaning artists may weigh the enormous exposure against the possibility of political controversy and intense public scrutiny.

The halftime performance has increasingly become a major cultural moment beyond music, placing its headliner under enormous attention. Recent shows featuring artists including Bad Bunny and Kendrick Lamar have generated extensive discussion, adding to the pressure surrounding whoever accepts the 2027 invitation.

With an announcement reportedly targeted for the end of September, the headliner search could remain unresolved for several more weeks.

articles.title: Will the NFL be able to convince Taylor Swift to perform at the Super Bowl LXI halftime show?
articles.standfirst: A Super Bowl in Nashville could give Swift the perfect stage — but not until 2030
articles.summary: A Super Bowl in Nashville could give Swift the perfect stage — but not until 2030
articles.body:
Taylor Swift remains one of the biggest names the NFL could possibly land for its Super Bowl halftime show, but the circumstances surrounding Super Bowl LXI may make a deal particularly difficult.

The 2027 championship game is scheduled for February 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, meaning it’ll take place on Valentine’s Day. That date could be a significant factor for Swift , especially following her marriage to Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce.

Swift and Kelce married on July 3, 2026, at Madison Square Garden, adding another layer to the singer’s connection with the NFL. With Kelce playing this season, the possibility of him playing in the Super Bowl would obviously change the situation.

However, at 36 and in his 14th NFL season, questions about his future have continued to follow the Chiefs tight end.

The NFL has reportedly continued to regard Swift as a dream halftime-show performer. Roc Nation, which works with the league on the entertainment strategy for the event, is also involved in the selection process.

Yet reports have consistently stressed that Swift ultimately controls whether she wants to accept such an opportunity.

Why 2027 may not be Swift’s year

Location could be another important consideration. Nashville has long been associated with Swift’s career, having played a major role in her development as a country and pop superstar. Reports have previously suggested that performing at a Super Bowl in Nashville would be particularly appealing to her.

That possibility now has a concrete date attached to it. The NFL has awarded Super Bowl LXIV to Nashville for 2030, with the game set to be played at the Tennessee Titans’ new stadium.

The decision makes Nashville a potential future destination for Swift if she eventually decides the Super Bowl stage is right for her.

That doesn’t mean Los Angeles is automatically ruled out. There’s currently no public confirmation that Swift has rejected an offer for Super Bowl LXI, nor has the NFL officially announced its halftime performer.

Swift also has plenty keeping her occupied away from football. Her latest music project, The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, is scheduled to add four tracks to her 2025 album. She’s also set to make a major appearance at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, where her “Patient Zero” video will premiere.

The video, directed by Swift , stars Colin Farrell and Dakota Johnson and will add another high-profile project to an already busy period in her career.

Swift would undoubtedly represent an enormous halftime attraction for the NFL. But with Valentine’s Day, Kelce’s ongoing career and the prospect of a future Super Bowl in Nashville, 2027 may not be the moment when the league finally gets its wish.
